title: Three-Project Solution Scaffold + IKeychainProvider
description: Create the complete solution structure with three projects, correct project references, build properties, and a fully implemented IKeychainProvider abstraction with all four concrete platform implementations.
prerequisiteState: Empty repository. Only tech_spec/ and .ai/ folders exist. No src/ directory yet.
goal: Produce a compilable three-project .NET 10 solution where IKeychainProvider is fully defined and all four implementations (macOS, Windows, Linux, encrypted-file fallback) are correctly wired with runtime platform detection.
scope: Create src/cliq-cli.sln referencing all four projects
Create src/CliqCli/CliqCli.csproj (net10.0, TreatWarningsAsErrors, Nullable enable, PublishSingleFile + self-contained flags in publish profile)
Create src/CliqCli.Core/CliqCli.Core.csproj (net10.0, TreatWarningsAsErrors, Nullable enable, no Spectre dependency)
Create tests/CliqCli.Tests/CliqCli.Tests.csproj (net10.0, xUnit, references CliqCli.Core and CliqCli.Keychain)
Set project references: CliqCli → Core + Keychain; Core → Keychain
Create src/CliqCli.Keychain/MacOsKeychainProvider.cs using Security.framework P/Invoke (SecKeychainAddGenericPassword / SecKeychainFindGenericPassword / SecKeychainItemDelete)
Create src/CliqCli.Keychain/LinuxKeychainProvider.cs using libsecret-1 via P/Invoke; catch DllNotFoundException to signal fallback needed
Create src/CliqCli.Keychain/EncryptedFileKeychainProvider.cs using AES-256-GCM with machine-entropy derived key (see OQ-002)

Create src/CliqCli.Keychain/KeychainProviderFactory.cs with static Create() method using RuntimeInformation.IsOSPlatform for platform selection and catching keychain unavailability to activate fallback
Create src/CliqCli/Program.cs stub (empty CommandApp, no commands yet)
Run dotnet build and confirm 0 errors, 0 warnings
acceptanceCriteria: dotnet build src/cliq-cli.sln succeeds with 0 errors and 0 warnings
IKeychainProvider interface is in CliqCli.Keychain namespace with exactly GetAsync, SetAsync, DeleteAsync signatures
All four IKeychainProvider implementations exist as separate classes in src/CliqCli.Keychain/
KeychainProviderFactory.Create() returns the correct implementation for the current OS
EncryptedFileKeychainProvider uses AES-256-GCM (not CBC or ECB)
No third-party NuGet keychain package is referenced in any .csproj
CliqCli.Core.csproj has zero reference to Spectre.Console
CliqCli.Keychain.csproj has zero reference to CliqCli.Core or CliqCli
TreatWarningsAsErrors=true and Nullable=enable present in all four .csproj files
In-memory fake IKeychainProvider implementation exists in tests/ for use by all other test stories
contextForAgent: This is the foundation story. Nothing else can be built until this passes. Read ADR-0009 for the three-project layout rationale and dependency graph. Read ADR-0003 for the full keychain design including P/Invoke details for each platform. Read ADR-0001 for .csproj build requirements. The key format is 'cliq-cli:<accountName>:<tokenType>' (e.g. 'cliq-cli:work:pat'). The encrypted-file fallback stores files at <configDir>/keystore/<accountName>.bin. For machine entropy key derivation, see OQ-002 default assumption. For Linux libsecret, see OQ-003.

openItems.item: Machine entropy key derivation for EncryptedFileKeychainProvider
openItems.defaultAssumption: See OQ-002. Use SHA256(MachineName + MachineGuid + 'cliq-cli') as AES-256 key. IV stored as first 12 bytes of .bin file.

See OQ-003. Catch DllNotFoundException when loading libsecret-1. Catch org.freedesktop.Secret errors. On any failure, return false from a TryInitialize() method. KeychainProviderFactory checks this and selects EncryptedFileKeychainProvider.

openItems.item: macOS keychain ACL on unsigned builds
openItems.defaultAssumption: Use kSecAttrAccessibleWhenUnlocked for access control. If the keychain returns errSecAuthFailed on a developer build, log the error and activate fallback.
